BiblicalUsage: Galal means to roll, and it rolls stones, bodies, and judgment alike. Jacob rolled the stone from the well's mouth in Genesis 29:10, and Saul told the people to roll a great stone to him in 1 Samuel 14:33. Amasa wallowed in blood in the highway in 2 Samuel 20:12, and Amos cries that judgment should run down as waters in Amos 5:24.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe rolling is the motion of God's work in the world. Stones roll away from wells so flocks can drink, and judgment rolls down like water so the land can be cleansed. I hold that the God who rolls stones away is the God who rolls our burdens away too.
